climate_flavour.note: Salt Spring: quality swings from year to year - aromatic and sweet in good years, 'flat and musty' in lesser ones.

american-mother.peak: de Wikipedia: ready to eat December-January; Scott Farm: not long keeping
american-mother.notes: Orange Pippin page (slug 'mother') only says 'rated for its flavor', no flavour words, so not counted. Banana is supported only by German Wikipedia's 'Lavanttaler Bananenapfel' article, which treats that Austrian name as American Mother. Scott Farm's 'balsamic' maps to no tag.

api.notes: Orange Pippin page is under the slug 'lady' (Lady Apple). en Wikipedia 'Api (apple)' and Scott Farm 'Lady Apple' pages have no flavour words. Salt Spring says it keeps well.

ashmeads-kernel.storage_change: Lemony and sharp when first picked; mellows and sweetens as sugars develop in store; flavours develop over time in storage.
ashmeads-kernel.peak: Pick late (mid Oct to late Nov); improves in store, keeping 3 months or more
ashmeads-kernel.notes: Scott Farm and Trees of Antiquity are both US nurseries (separate organisations). Nobody here says 'earthy'.

bardsey.notes: Orange Pippin has no prose tasting notes, only the 'sharper' style field; 'lightly lemon-scented' there is a user comment (not used). enlli.org is the Bardsey Island Trust. Cooksinfo says it does not store well. Not in NFC.

belle-de-boskoop.storage_change: Sharp at picking; sweetens in storage or if left hanging late on the tree (Trees of Antiquity); tastes better after some time in storage, keeping six months chilled (Salt Spring).
belle-de-boskoop.notes: No modern source here mentions honey. Salt Spring calls it 'sweet, subacid', against every other source's tart/very acid.

bess-pool.notes: No modern source supports 'wine'. No en Wikipedia page.

bloody-ploughman.peak: Walcot: pick mid September, keeps until November
bloody-ploughman.notes: Orange Pippin's prose says 'mild but sweet' while its flavour-style field says 'sharper' - internally inconsistent. No source supports 'berry'.

braeburn.storage_change: Orange Pippin: arguably best soon after picking rather than improving in store; pear-drop hint is in new-season fruit. Wikipedia notes a browning disorder in long storage.

climate_flavour.note: Needs a warmer climate and longer season; NFC says fruit usually fails to mature fully in the UK.

braeburn.peak: Soon after picking; best served slightly below room temperature (Orange Pippin)

caroline.notes: Apples & Orchards (applesandorchards.org.uk/product/caroline/) describes only 'crisp and firm fleshed', long-keeping - no flavour words. Not on Orange Pippin.

chestnut-crab.peak: Scott Farm: long ripening period, early Sep to late Oct
chestnut-crab.notes: Not on Orange Pippin (its crab-apple page redirects to the home page); NFC lists 'Chestnut' but holds no material/description. No source here mentions wine.

court-pendu-plat.storage_change: Fruity and strong at picking; sweetens and mellows by Christmas; flavour ripens through early winter in store.
court-pendu-plat.peak: From Christmas into early winter; keeps to about March (Walcot)
court-pendu-plat.notes: No source here says 'spice'. Walcot's 'pineapple-like acidity' is a lone note.

crimson-peasgood.notes: NFC page (id 1376) says only 'Fruits cook well' - no flavour words. Not on Orange Pippin.

climate_flavour.note: Orange Pippin: should not be picked in the UK until late November, perhaps suggesting a warmer-climate origin.

decio.peak: Keeps well into the following year (Orange Pippin)

edward-vii.peak: Walcot: pick mid October, keeps until April

emperor-alexander.storage_change: Crisp at harvest, becoming softer and crumblier in storage (Aport article); keeps only 2-3 weeks per Orange Pippin.

climate_flavour.note: Aport article: growers credit the soil and altitude of the Almaty foothills for its strong honey-like aroma; seedlings unremarkable elsewhere.

emperor-alexander.notes: Sources disagree sharply: NFC (as 'Alexander') finds coarse, dry, acid flesh with very little flavour; Orange Pippin and Salt Spring a soft sweet-sharp cooker; German Wikipedia (quoting an old description) a spicy, raspberry-like, winey sweet apple; the en Wikipedia 'Aport' article gives honey, hazelnut and anise, but describes Almaty-grown Aport, which may not be the same clone as the western Emperor Alexander.

falstaff.storage_change: Crunchy and sharp off the tree; mellows and softens somewhat with age but stays juicy (Orange Pippin).
falstaff.peak: Straight from the tree (Orange Pippin); keeps 1-2 months

francis.storage_change: Can become more complex in store (Apples & Orchards).
francis.notes: Sources disagree on sweetness: NFC 'very sweet', Apples & Orchards 'not particularly sweet'. Not on Orange Pippin.

gala.storage_change: Freshly picked fruit is punchier and pear-like (Orange Pippin); stored fruit tastes slightly less sweet than in-season fruit (Wikipedia).
gala.notes: Pear note only from Orange Pippin (freshly picked fruit).

climate_flavour.note: German Wikipedia: good fruit quality depends on crop load and a mild climate.

glockenapfel.peak: Picked October, ready to eat from December; keeps in cold store until June (de/en Wikipedia)
glockenapfel.notes: en and de Wikipedia counted as two sources (separate articles). Orange Pippin page has no tasting notes; its only flavour words are a visitor comment ('mild, not too much sweetness'), not used.

golden-noble.notes: Apples & Orchards (applesandorchards.org.uk/product/golden-noble/) adds only 'cooks to a slightly acidic puree'.

gravenstein.storage_change: Does not keep (about a week, Orange Pippin); its distinctive aroma is lost in cold or ordinary CA storage (en Wikipedia); flesh turns mealy with longer storage (de Wikipedia).
gravenstein.peak: Straight from the tree, mid-Aug to mid-Sep (Scott Farm)
gravenstein.notes: Single-source notes: berry (Scott Farm), savoury (Salt Spring), spicy (de Wikipedia).

hamids-red-pippin.peak: Orange Pippin: picked late Sep-Oct, keeps 2-3 weeks
hamids-red-pippin.notes: Only source found. Other descriptions online trace to the raiser, Keepers Nursery, which we may not use.

hewes-crab.peak: Big Horse Creek: ripens Sep-Oct and is a good keeper
hewes-crab.notes: Orange Pippin's crab-apple page redirects to the home page; not in NFC. No source here uses 'bitter'. Scott Farm's butterscotch/banana is a lone note.

hubbardston-nonesuch.storage_change: Salt Spring: the light flavour sweetens with increasing ripeness.

jelly-king.notes: No flavour description found: Orange Pippin crab-apple page redirects to the home page; Walcot and Leafland (NZ) pages describe only colour, size and jelly use.

jupiter.notes: en Wikipedia 'Jupiter (apple)' only paraphrases Orange Pippin, so not counted.

kermerrien.peak: Salt Spring: about three weeks of sweating at most
kermerrien.notes: Contradiction: Orange Pippin calls it an acidic (sharp) blending apple; French Wikipedia and Salt Spring call it bitter/bittersweet. No source here says astringent.

knobby-russet.notes: Texture disagrees: NFC firm and rather dry, Wikipedia soft and creamy. Not on Orange Pippin.

landsberger-reinette.peak: de Wikipedia: ripe from November, keeps to end of January
landsberger-reinette.notes: Texture disagrees (NFC soft, de Wikipedia firm). Scott Farm page says only 'soft, juicy flesh'. en Wikipedia has no flavour words. Not on Orange Pippin.

ligol.storage_change: Flesh stays firm a long time in store (Polish Wikipedia).
ligol.peak: Picked early October in Poland, eating-ripe a few weeks later; keeps to Feb-Mar (Apr in CA)
ligol.notes: Not on Orange Pippin or NFC; specialtyproduce.com and inhort.pl could not be fetched.

lord-derby.storage_change: Acidic if picked young, milder once fully ripe and yellowing (Orange Pippin).

michelin.notes: Wikipedia says high tannins, Salt Spring 'soft tannins'.

newtown-pippin.storage_change: Hard and unappetising off the tree; needs 1-2 months in store to develop (Orange Pippin, Wikipedia); develops full sugar and rich flavour after storage (Trees of Antiquity).

climate_flavour.note: Needs a hot summer and autumn; will not ripen properly most years in England (Orange Pippin); does great in warm summer locations (Trees of Antiquity).

newtown-pippin.peak: Over winter after 1-2 months in store
newtown-pippin.notes: No source here says 'wine'. Pineapple only from Salt Spring ('some equate to'); 'piney' (Wikipedia, Trees of Antiquity) maps to no tag.

nuvar-cheerfull-gold.peak: Orange Pippin: late picking, keeps 3 months or more
nuvar-cheerfull-gold.notes: Orange Pippin page slug is 'cheerfull-gold'. Not in NFC.

pepin-shafranny.storage_change: Salt Spring: tastes good only for a few weeks after its late-August harvest; the Latvian Institute of Horticulture says it stores well.
pepin-shafranny.peak: Late Aug-Sep, soon after picking (Salt Spring)
pepin-shafranny.notes: No modern source found supporting wine, spice or sweet; descriptions are about texture only. Storage reports conflict.

polka.notes: NFC entry is under the synonym 'Trajan'.

priscilla.notes: Orange Pippin classes it 'sharper', Salt Spring 'mildly subacid'. NFC 'perfumed' is not in our tags.

raxao.notes: Only source found (es Wikipedia, which also gives total acidity 5.3 g/l).

red-sentinel.notes: No flavour description found: Walcot describes only colour, persistence and bird food; Orange Pippin crab-apple page redirects to the home page; NFC page has no description.

rhode-island-greening.storage_change: Tart when freshly picked (best for cooking); mellows in store into a rich eating apple, keeping into spring (Salt Spring, Wikipedia).
rhode-island-greening.peak: Cook from picking; eat fresh after storage
rhode-island-greening.notes: No source here mentions lemon or grape.

royal-gala.storage_change: Cold-stored fruit tastes slightly less sweet than in-season fruit (Wikipedia Gala article).
royal-gala.notes: Wikipedia 'Royal Gala' redirects to the Gala article, so this is the parent's description. Orange Pippin's Royal Gala page has no flavour words. No source mentions floral.

sam-young.notes: Orange Pippin page has no tasting notes ('Medium. Russet.').

sekai-ichi.notes: Texture differs: Orange Pippin crisp, Wikipedia 'not as crisp', Salt Spring 'fairly soft'.

signe-tillisch.peak: de Wikipedia: picked early October, keeps until Christmas

sops-in-wine.notes: Orange Pippin's 'sweet but not rich' is in its References section (an older quoted description); its style field says 'sharper'. NFC holds two different clones; (1) used.

sweet-alford.notes: Walcot says 'no astringency' (our summary says faint astringency; not a tag). Not in NFC.

tolman-sweet.peak: Wikipedia (1905 data): in ordinary storage November-January
tolman-sweet.notes: Juiciness disputed: Big Horse Creek 'juicy', others dry.

vista-bella.storage_change: Flavour and crispness decay very rapidly after picking (Orange Pippin); eat within a few days (Salt Spring).
vista-bella.peak: Straight from the tree; keep in the fridge and serve cool (Orange Pippin)

wickson-crab.peak: Salt Spring: late October; keeps about 2 months refrigerated
wickson-crab.notes: Contradiction on acidity: Scott Farm 'just a touch of acidity' vs Salt Spring 'big-time acids'. No source here says astringent. Orange Pippin crab page redirects to home.

climate_flavour.note: Trees of Antiquity: mostly for baking, but in the right climate on sandy soil it becomes a good dessert apple.

wolf-river.notes: Orange Pippin's visitor comments (not used) say it needs a frost to reach full flavour.

yellow-bellflower.storage_change: Acidic early in the season; picked tart and mellowed in storage, becoming a good dessert apple later (Trees of Antiquity, Orange Pippin).
yellow-bellflower.peak: Later in the season after storage
yellow-bellflower.notes: en Wikipedia has no flavour words. No source mentions citrus/lime. Orange Pippin's style list is its tasting-notes summary.
